Bessent reportedly moves to military base over Iranian threats; Hegseth: 'crazy Islamists in Tehran will never have a nuclear weapon'; House blocks Hegseth impeachment bid 211–204; oil rebounds — Brent ~$93.87 (+2.60%), WTI ~$87.94 (+2.21%) as Iran denies any talks; gold falls below $4,000 to ~$3,987 — analysts warn of further losses toward $3,900; Dow +0.49%, S&P +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%; US gas drops to $3.94/gal (AAA) — largest one-day drop in 18 years, first time below $4 since war began; heating oil surges 4.1% after Ukrainian drone strike causes fire at Russia's Ust-Luga export hub; Allianz Trade: Gulf war damage exceeds $200B, cumulative losses $790B (5.9% GDP gap) through 2030 — 80+ energy facilities struck; Saudi coalition destroys 2 Houthi drones toward Mecca region — Houthis deny targeting holy city; Saudi Civil Defence alerts Taif, Yanbu, Khamis Mushait; 2 missiles intercepted over Saudi Arabia; fire at Iran's South Pars gas field overnight — cause unknown; PGSA: 'non-compliant' vessels can reduce penalties by acknowledging violations; CENTCOM: 'strictly enforcing ironclad naval blockade'; Aramco and QatarEnergy offer crude via tenders; Iran FM Araghchi condemns US $20M nuclear reward offer — urges UNSC and IAEA to condemn; three men charged over alleged Iran-linked plot against RAF Fairford; Pezeshkian: US and Israel dealing with political fallout from military conflicts; Saudi Arabia led further jump in OPEC+ output; UAE flight disruptions continue — Etihad cancels Abu Dhabi–Riyadh/Dammam through Nov 19

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 258 as diplomatic momentum stalled and Iran publicly hardened its negotiating posture. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Tehran's chief negotiator, told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview that the strait will 'never return' to its pre-war status, declaring that 'the ball is now in the American court.' Ghalibaf revealed that Iran and Oman had reached an understanding to jointly oversee the waterway — part of Tehran's seven-point proposal — and flatly rejected the concept of 'free waters' in the strait, arguing that the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea does not apply and that the bordering states' laws govern transit. Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei called reports of a recent US-Iran meeting in Qatar 'pure lies' designed to push down oil prices, and vowed that 'not even a single particle of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran' — a direct rejection of Washington's core demand for any final deal. The IRGC unveiled a new underground missile facility, publishing images of ballistic and cruise missiles through Tasnim News Agency, while Rezaei separately threatened to strike US bases in Europe if they were used for attacks against Iran. Iran also designated Argentina's navy and air force as 'terrorist organizations,' escalating the diplomatic confrontation with Buenos Aires. In Washington, the House voted 211–204 to refer Representative Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively halting the effort. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly moved from his home to a military base amid Iranian threats, while Hegseth declared that 'crazy Islamists in Tehran will never ever have a nuclear weapon.' Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi condemned a US offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear facilities and urged the UN Security Council and IAEA to condemn it, while Secretary of State Rubio rejected Iran's demand for war reparations.

Markets rebounded sharply on Wednesday as Iran's denial of any ongoing negotiations jolted the war-risk premium back into oil prices. Brent crude rose approximately 2.60% to settle around $93.87/bbl, reversing Tuesday's slide to two-month lows, while WTI climbed roughly 2.21% to $87.94/bbl. Rezaei's characterization of peace talks as 'pure lies' undercut the de-escalation narrative that had driven Brent down 22% from its October 30 peak of $117.64. Heating oil surged 4.1% after a Ukrainian drone strike caused a fire at Russia's Ust-Luga export hub, adding to energy supply fears. Despite the oil rebound, US gasoline prices continued their descent, dropping to $3.94/gal (AAA) — the largest single-day drop in 18 years and the first time below $4 since the war began. Gold fell further below the critical $4,000 level, trading at approximately $3,987/oz as the hot CPI data continued to weigh — CME FedWatch now shows a 13.2% probability of a 50bp December hike alongside a fully priced 25bp increase. Analysts at TD Securities warned of a retest of support near $3,900. Stocks rallied: the Dow climbed 0.49% to 52,486, the S&P 500 gained 1.31% to 7,619, and the Nasdaq surged 1.60% to 25,466. Newcastle coal held near $145/tonne. VLCC rates for Arabian Gulf–China routes continued to soften into the $340K–380K/day range as the overall trend of easing war premiums offset the single-day oil bounce. Allianz Trade released a comprehensive assessment of the war's economic toll: more than $200 billion in physical damage across GCC countries, with more than 80 energy facilities struck — mostly in Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain — and a third severely damaged. The insurer projects cumulative economic losses of $790 billion, representing a 5.9% GDP gap versus pre-war trend, through 2030.

The maritime situation in the Strait of Hormuz showed no signs of improvement despite the diplomatic posturing. The IRGC claimed on Wednesday that two more oil tankers struck sea mines and caught fire while attempting what it called an 'unauthorized and hazardous route' through the strait — continuing its near-daily pattern of mine-strike claims. This followed Tuesday's confirmed attack on the Liberia-flagged supertanker MT Fujairah Energy, which was hit by a projectile in the Arabian Gulf, injuring four crew members including one Indian national with minor injuries. Six Indian seafarers were aboard; India's external affairs minister confirmed all were safe. UKMTO had separately reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile near Lima, Oman (Warning 201-26), along with an additional later tanker incident with crew and damage status unknown. Reuters tallied 37 ship attacks in October — the war's highest monthly total — with 10 more already recorded in November as of reporting. CENTCOM declared it was 'strictly enforcing the ironclad naval blockade against Iran' and keeping Hormuz open to commercial shipping. The Saudi-led coalition destroyed two Houthi drones launched toward the Mecca region and southern areas on Wednesday evening, with the Houthis denying they targeted the holy city. Saudi Civil Defence issued alerts for Taif, Yanbu, and Khamis Mushait, though authorities later said the danger had passed; two additional missiles were intercepted over Saudi Arabia. A fire was reported at Iran's South Pars gas field overnight — cause unknown. The PGSA announced that 'non-compliant' vessels could reduce penalties by acknowledging violations, suggesting a formalization of Iran's transit-permission regime. UAE flight disruptions continued, with Etihad cancelling Abu Dhabi flights to Riyadh and Dammam through November 19, and Emirates, flydubai, and Air Arabia also reporting Saudi route cancellations.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. European Commission: fertilizer-to-cereal price ratios at weakest since 2022. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Fertilizer ships face long backlog even if Hormuz reopens — access not cost will define markets (Supply Chain Brain/World Fertilizer). Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.
